textbookText: 7.7 Gravitational potential Energy Activity 7.4 xxii) Take a ball and throw it in the air and watch the motion of the ball Take a ball and throw it into the air, then observe its motion. Consider what happens to the kinetic energy (K.E.) you imparted to the ball upon throwing it, and why its speed gradually decreases. The kinetic energy converts into gravitational potential energy (P.E.), and the decrease in speed of the ball is due to the influence of Earth’s gravitational field. When the ball is thrown, it possesses kinetic energy and experiences acceleration, resulting in a force acting on it.

One can express the change in energy (∆E) as ∆E = mg∆x, where ∆x represents the change in distance (or height), and for a large distance, we use ∆x, while for a small range, we use h. When considering the change in energy between a distance r and infinity, we get ∆E = f.dr.

Therefore, one can define gravitational potential energy as follows: The gravitational potential energy of a body at any point within a gravitational field is the amount of work required to bring the body from infinity to that point without causing acceleration. As described in the previous article, let us consider a body of mass ‘m’ lying at a point of infinity from the center of the Earth at radius R and mass m supposed to be concentrated at its center.

7.8 Variation of Acceleration due to Gravity Observe the following activities: xxiii) A body that is difficult to lift at the bottom of a high hill is easier to lift at the top. xxiv) The same body weighs more near the pole than near the equator
Physics, Grade 11 | 162

xxv) A body thrown upwards decreases its velocity with each passing second, and the final velocity becomes zero at its maximum height. xxvi) It is difficult to stop while running downhill, and our velocity increases with every passing second. Similar phenomena claim that there is a variation in the value of acceleration due to gravity based on points on the Earth, which is fully illustrated below.

7.8.2 Variation of g with depth When a body lies within the Earth's surface, the part of the Earth above it doesn’t contribute to the mass of the Earth. Only the part beneath and including the body contributes to it. Hence, the mass of the Earth decreases, which in turn tries to decrease the value of acceleration.
